q: What is a quality attribute?
short: A measurable or testable property (non-functional requirement) specifying how well a system meets stakeholder needs along a dimension, qualifying functional requirements: e.g. performance, availability, usability.

q: Group the common quality attributes.
short: Operational: availability, performance, scalability, reliability. Structural: portability, maintainability, configurability, extensibility. Cross-cutting: security, usability, accessibility, legal.
detail: Keep the list short and relevant.

q: What makes a quality requirement SMART?
short: Specific, Measurable, Attainable, Relevant, Time-sensitive (bounded by period or conditions), e.g. order placement within 3 s for 95% of peak requests.

q: Which quality attributes are specific to ML components?
short: Accuracy, robustness, explainability, fairness, data-drift adaptability, model-drift monitoring, reproducibility (plus scalability, reliability, maintainability, security/privacy).
detail: Shaped by problem type, approach, training, data.

q: What is robustness for an ML model? Give examples.
short: Keeping performance under noisy, incomplete or adversarial inputs: fraud detection with missing fields, pedestrian detection in rain/fog/poor light, speech recognition with background noise.

q: Software vs system architecture?
short: Software architecture: structures of software elements, their visible properties and relationships. System architecture adds hardware, AI/ML, infrastructure and communication components.
example: Bipolar-monitoring system with sensors, gateway, cloud ML.

q: What is an architectural pattern?
short: A general, reusable solution to a recurring architectural problem in a context, with defined roles and relationships, expressed as {context, problem, solution}; e.g. MVC, pipe-and-filter, microservices.

q: Explain the pipe-and-filter pattern.
short: A system as a sequence of independent filters, each transforming data, connected by pipes from a source to a sink; promotes modularity and reuse because filters can be swapped or reordered.

q: Why did the flash sale fail and the streaming event succeed?
short: The streaming platform identified scalability and performance as key quality attributes and built a matching architecture (microservices on Kubernetes); the sale site didn't design for its peak.
follow: What would you change for the sale?

q: List the components of a RAG enterprise chatbot.
short: Software (auth, API gateway, orchestration), hardware/infra (cloud servers, GPUs, storage), data (vector DB, document store, logs DB), ML (embedder, retriever, LLM, re-ranker), deployment (Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD).

q: Write SMART quality requirements for a fraud-scoring API.
short: p99 latency ≤ 50 ms at 5,000 TPS; 99.99% availability monthly; recall ≥ 0.9 at precision ≥ 0.6 on monthly holdout; retraining within 48 h of drift alert; top-3 reason codes for every decline; PII never leaves region.

q: How do quality attributes drive architecture? Give an example.
short: Each QA suggests tactics/patterns: scalability → stateless services and autoscaling; availability → redundancy and failover; latency → caching, co-location, smaller models; modifiability → modular boundaries; explainability → interpretable model or explanation service.

q: A fraud model was trained 18 months ago and now needs urgent retraining. Which QAs were missing?
short: Repeatability, retrainability, operability, monitorability, explainability, maintainability, deployability, data completeness/consistency.
example: Legacy code, data issues, ad hoc MLOps.
mistakes: Treating it as a one-off fix.

q: Privacy vs operating cost vs monitoring: how do they conflict in fraud detection?
short: Comprehensive monitoring wants more data collected and moved; privacy limits collection and transfer; storing and moving data costs money. Balance with aggregation, minimisation, regional processing and sampling.

q: What does 'separate ML and non-ML responsibilities' mean?
short: ML components only infer; non-ML code does orchestration, validation, business rules, user interaction, logging and fallbacks. Clear interfaces let each evolve and be tested independently.
example: Rules veto a model's approval above a limit.
mistakes: Business rules hidden in model features.

q: Implement a pipe-and-filter pipeline in Python.
short: Write each filter as a pure function (input → output); compose with a pipeline(*filters) helper or scikit-learn Pipeline; keep configuration outside filters; test each filter separately.

q: What groups appear in an ML software quality model?
short: Utility, economy, robustness, modifiability, productionisability (deployability, repeatability, operability, monitoring), comprehensibility (discoverability, traceability, debuggability…), responsibility (explainability, fairness, ownership, compliance, vulnerability).

q: How do you verify an availability requirement of 99.95%?
short: Define what counts as down (SLIs), measure via synthetic probes and real traffic, compute monthly/annual uptime, compare to error budget (≈263 min/yr), and alert when burn rate is high.

q: How do ML quality attributes interact and conflict?
short: Accuracy vs latency/cost (bigger models), accuracy vs explainability, fairness vs accuracy on some metrics, robustness vs accuracy on clean data, privacy vs monitoring, reproducibility vs freshness; resolve with explicit priorities and tests.

q: Design an architecture for an e-commerce site's sale-day peak with an ML recommender.
short: Stateless web tier with autoscaling; queue-based order processing; inventory with strong consistency; recommender as separate service with cache and fallback to popular items; pre-warm capacity; rate limiting; load tests at 2× forecast; observability and graceful degradation.

q: What are the drawbacks of pipe-and-filter?
short: Latency and data copying between stages, difficulty with interactive/stateful processing, error handling across stages, possible lowest-common-denominator data formats, and need for orchestration and monitoring per filter.

q: How do you make reproducibility a testable requirement?
short: Require pinned code, data snapshot, environment and seeds; re-run training in CI on a sample and assert metrics within tolerance; store lineage; fail builds when non-determinism exceeds bounds.

q: How would you evaluate robustness as a quality attribute?
short: Define perturbation families (noise, missing fields, weather, adversarial), set acceptable degradation (e.g. ≤ 5 points recall), build stress test sets, track per-slice metrics, and monitor production input quality.
follow: How do you get fog data?

q: Your architecture must support continuous model evolution. What do you design in?
short: Model registry and versioned artifacts, feature store or shared feature code, automated retraining pipelines, evaluation gates, canary/shadow deployment, monitoring and drift detection, rollback, interfaces that hide model versions from clients.
follow: How do clients handle schema changes?
mistakes: Hard-coding a model file in the app.
